arxiv-2012-07682.title: The strongly intensive observable in pp collisions at LHC energies in the string fusion model
arxiv-2012-07682.creator: V V Vechernin 1, S N Belokurova 1
arxiv-2012-07682.description: Abstract The properties of the strongly intensive variable characterizing correlations between the number of particles in two separated rapidity interval in pp interactions at LHC energies are studied in the framework of the string fusion model. We perform the MC simulations of string distributions in the impact parameter plane to take into account the experimental conditions of pp collisions.

arxiv-2207-01327.title: BoAT v2 - A Web-Based Dependency Annotation Tool with Focus on Agglutinative Languages
arxiv-2207-01327.creator: Salih Furkan Akkurt, Büşra Marşan, Susan Uskudarli
arxiv-2207-01327.description: Abstract The value of quality treebanks is steadily increasing due to the crucial role they play in the development of natural language processing tools. The creation of such treebanks is enormously labor-intensive and time-consuming. Especially when the size of treebanks is considered, tools that support the annotation process are essential.

arxiv-2303-17268.title: Classical-to-quantum non-signalling boxes
arxiv-2303-17268.creator: Carolina Moreira Ferrera, Robin Simmons, James Purcell, Daniel Collins, Sandu Popescu
arxiv-2303-17268.description: Abstract Here we introduce the concept of classical input - quantum output (C-Q) non-signalling boxes, a generalisation of the classical input - classical output (C-C) non-signalling boxes. We argue that studying such objects leads to a better understanding of the relation between quantum nonlocality and non-locality beyond quantum mechanics.

arxiv-2401-03383.title: On the Ehrhart Theory of Generalized Symmetric Edge Polytopes
arxiv-2401-03383.creator: Robert Davis, Akihiro Higashitani, Hidefumi Ohsugi
arxiv-2401-03383.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Robert Davis, Akihiro Higashitani, Hidefumi Ohsugi. The symmetric edge polytope (SEP) of a (finite, undirected) graph is a centrally symmetric lattice polytope whose vertices are defined by the edges of the graph. SEPs have been studied extensively in the past twenty years. Recently, Tóthmérész and, independently, D’Alí, Juhnke-Kubitzke, and Koch generalized the definition of an SEP to regular matroids, which are the matroids that can be represented by totally unimodular matrices.

arxiv-2407-18103.title: Fine-Tuning Large Language Models for Stock Return Prediction Using Newsflow
arxiv-2407-18103.creator: Tian Guo Emmanuel Hauptmann
arxiv-2407-18103.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) and their fine-tuning techniques have demonstrated superior performance in various language understanding and generation tasks. This paper explores fine-tuning LLMs for stock return forecasting with financial newsflow. In quantitative investing, return forecasting is fundamental for subsequent tasks like stock picking, portfolio optimization, etc. We formulate the model to include text representation and forecasting modules.

arxiv-2504-19559.title: Using the Translation Theorem for the Automated Stationkeeping of Extremely-Low Lunar Missions
arxiv-2504-19559.creator: Jack Yarndley, Martin Lara, Harry Holt, Roberto Armellin
arxiv-2504-19559.description: Abstract Extremely-Low Lunar Orbits (eLLOs) (altitudes ≤ 50 \leq 50 km) exhibit severe perturbations due to the highly non-spherical lunar gravitational field, presenting unique challenges to orbit maintenance. These altitudes are too low for the existence of stable ‘frozen’ orbits, and naive stationkeeping methods, such as circularization, perform poorly.

arxiv-2510-12773.title: Dr.LLM: Dynamic Layer Routing in LLMs
arxiv-2510-12773.creator: Ahmed Heakl, Martin Gubri, Salman Khan, Sangdoo Yun, Seong Joon Oh
arxiv-2510-12773.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) process every token through all layers of a transformer stack, causing wasted computation on simple queries and insufficient flexibility for harder ones that need deeper reasoning. Adaptive-depth methods can improve efficiency, but prior approaches rely on costly inference-time search, architectural changes, or large-scale retraining, and in practice often degrade accuracy despite efficiency gains.

arxiv-2512-22123.title: A Study of NP-Completeness and Undecidable Word Problems in Semigroups
arxiv-2512-22123.creator: Duaa Abdullah, Jasem Hamoud
arxiv-2512-22123.description: Abstract In this paper we explore fundamental concepts in computational complexity theory and the boundaries of algorithmic decidability. We examine the relationship between complexity classes P and NP , where L ∈ P L\in\textbf{P} implies the existence of a deterministic Turing machine solving L L in polynomial time O ⁡ ( n k ) O(n^{k}) .

The clinical course of many renal diseases, and thereby of CKD, is highly variable. One of the major challenges in deciding which treatment approach is best suited...

pmc-10690476.title: Pancreatic Replacement Therapy for Maladaptive Behaviors in Preschool Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder
pmc-10690476.creator: Deborah A. Pearson, Robert L. Hendren, Matthew F. Heil, William R. McIntyre, Shane R. Raines
pmc-10690476.description: This cohort study evaluates the use of pancreatic replacement therapy for maladaptive behaviors in preschool children with autism spectrum disorder. Introduction Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder in which individuals demonstrate persistent core deficits in social communication and social interaction along with restricted, repetitive patterns of behavior, interests, or activities.

pmc-10744364.title: Quantitative Electroencephalography Markers for an Accurate Diagnosis of Frontotemporal Dementia: A Spectral Power Ratio Approach
pmc-10744364.creator: Jinwon Chang, Chul Chang, Lucia Billeci
pmc-10744364.description: Background and Objectives: Frontotemporal dementia (FTD) is the second most common form of presenile dementia; however, its diagnosis has been poorly investigated. Previous attempts to diagnose FTD using quantitative electroencephalography (qEEG) have yielded inconsistent results in both spectral and functional connectivity analyses.

pmc-11420443.title: Associations of socioeconomic status and healthy lifestyle with incident dementia and cognitive decline: two prospective cohort studies
pmc-11420443.creator: Kan Wang, Yuan Fang, Ruizhi Zheng, Xuan Zhao, Siyu Wang, Jieli Lu, Weiqing Wang, Guang Ning, Yu Xu, Yufang Bi
pmc-11420443.description: SummaryBackgroundLittle is known about the complex associations of socioeconomic status (SES) and healthy lifestyle with cognitive dysfunction.MethodsUsing data from the Health and Retirement Study (HRS) [2008–2020] and the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA) [2004–2018], SES was constructed by latent class analysis using education level, total household income and wealth.

pmc-11526378.title: Float-Cast Microsieves with Elliptical Pores
pmc-11526378.creator: Nadine Schwaar, Dominik Benke, Markus Retsch, Werner A. Goedel
pmc-11526378.description: Polymeric microsieves bearing elliptical pores were successfully prepared via float-casting: a dispersion comprising nonvolatile acrylate monomers and ellipsoidal polystyrene particles was spread onto a water surface. The resulting self-organized monolayer was laterally compressed, and the monomer was photopolymerized, giving rise to a membrane comprising ellipsoidal particles laterally embedded in a 0.5 μm thin polymer membrane.

pmc-12551308.title: COVID-19 mortality among people living with HIV/AIDS in Brazil: a multilevel analysis
pmc-12551308.creator: Tatyellen Natasha da Costa Oliveira, Mariana Jorge de Queiroz, Anderson Lineu Siqueira dos Santos, Cleber Nascimento do Carmo, Geraldo Marcelo Cunha, Iuri da Costa Leite, Antonio Guilherme Pacheco
pmc-12551308.description: BackgroundThe simultaneous COVID-19 and HIV/AIDS pandemics have created unprecedented challenges, disrupting healthcare for people living with HIV/AIDS (PLWHA) and introducing an additional lethal threat. However, the impact of COVID-19 among PLWHA in Brazil remains unclear. We aimed to investigate the association between HIV infection and COVID-19 mortality in the Brazilian population.

pmc-12648772.title: Socio-cultural factors shaping complementary feeding initiation: a contextual analysis of maternal education, employment, and family support
pmc-12648772.creator: Kaan Celebier, Metin Yigit, Furkan Kalayci, Enes Kaan Kilic, Orkun Tolunay
pmc-12648772.description: BackgroundComplementary feeding represents a critical milestone in infant nutrition, where appropriate timing and informed decision-making are of great importance. Maternal factors such as education level, socioeconomic status, cultural values, and access to information sources play a significant role in shaping complementary feeding practices.
